statement: Inverse width recovers the actual two-piece likelihood at the held mean.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (x : Fin n → ℝ) (μ : ℝ) {w u : ℝ} (hu : 0 < u) : heldMeanSkew x μ w u = logLik x (μ - halfMean * ((1 - w) / u - w / u)) (w / u) ((1 - w) / u)

statement: With all data at the held mean, the Gaussian exponent is constant throughout the positive inverse-width ray and log likelihood is unbounded.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {μ w : ℝ} (hx : ∀ i, x i = μ) : Tendsto (heldMeanSkew x μ w) atTop atTop

statement: A nonzero residual gives exactly one finite maximizing scale when mean and skew are held. The scale is represented by inverse total width.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {μ w : ℝ} (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (hx : ∃ i, x i ≠ μ) : ∃! u, u ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ) ∧ IsMaxOn (heldMeanSkew x μ w) (Ioi 0) u

statement: The held-mean and held-skew likelihood attains its maximum exactly when the sample contains a nonzero residual from the mean.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {μ w : ℝ} (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) : (∃ u ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ), IsMaxOn (heldMeanSkew x μ w) (Ioi 0) u) ↔ ∃ i, x i ≠ μ

statement: For positive fixed scale and skew, the log likelihood tends to minus infinity at both location ends and admits exactly one maximizing mean. The shape of the sample is unrestricted.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {w u : ℝ} (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (hu : 0 < u) : Tendsto (fun μ ↦ heldMeanSkew x μ w u) (cocompact ℝ) atBot ∧ ∃! μ, IsMaxOn (fun m ↦ heldMeanSkew x m w u) univ μ

statement: If the sample is constant, the fixed-skew model has a collapsing path at its common observation, expressed in inverse total width.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {c : ℝ} (w : ℝ) (hx : ∀ i, x i = c) : Tendsto (fun u ↦ logLik x c (w / u) ((1 - w) / u)) atTop atTop

statement: With skew held, nonconstant data give exactly one joint maximizer and constant data have no finite maximizer.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {w : ℝ} (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) : ((∃ p ∈ LocationScale.domain, IsMaxOn (heldSkew x w) LocationScale.domain p) ↔ LocationScale.Nonconstant x) ∧ (LocationScale.Nonconstant x → ∃! p, p ∈ LocationScale.domain ∧ IsMaxOn (heldSkew x w) LocationScale.domain p)

statement: The all-free finite maximizing graph over mode, left width fraction and total width. This describes every tie for a nonconstant sample.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) {c w s : ℝ} (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (hs : 0 < s) : (∀ (d v t : ℝ), v ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 → 0 < t → heldSkew x v (d, t) ≤ heldSkew x w (c, s)) ↔ IsMinOn (modeProfile x) univ c ∧ w = modeFraction x c ∧ s = sqrt (modeProfile x c / n)
dossier_scope_note: Nonconstant branch. Reconstructed side scales are w*s and (1-w)*s.

statement: A bracketed mode is a mode strictly between the sample extremes. The all-free fit exists exactly when there is a bracketed minimizing mode. This condition also excludes every constant sample.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : (∃ c w s : ℝ, w ∈ Ioo 0 1 ∧ 0 < s ∧ ∀ (d v t : ℝ), v ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 → 0 < t → heldSkew x v (d, t) ≤ heldSkew x w (c, s)) ↔ ∃ c : ℝ, (∃ i, x i < c) ∧ (∃ j, c < x j) ∧ IsMinOn (modeProfile x) univ c

statement: A half-normal path at any supporting endpoint has its unpenalized trace. Its value is the all-free supremum exactly when that endpoint minimizes the mode profile. The endpoint RMS fixes its positive scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) (c : ℝ) (left : Bool) (hsupp : if left then ∀ j, x j ≤ c else ∀ j, c ≤ x j) : let b := sqrt (endpointSquares x c / n) Tendsto (fun w ↦ heldSkew x w (c,b)) (𝓝[Ioo 0 1] (if left then 1 else 0)) (𝓝 (halfLogLik x c b)) ∧ (IsLUB (allFreeValues x) (halfLogLik x c b) ↔ IsMinOn (modeProfile x) univ c)
dossier_scope_note: Joint log-likelihood trace and exact face comparison. Distributional convergence is a separate claim.

statement: Without an interior minimizing mode, the all-free supremum is a half-normal trace at a sample extreme. Both orientations are allowed.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) (hmiss : ¬ ∃ c : ℝ, (∃ i, x i < c) ∧ (∃ j, c < x j) ∧ IsMinOn (modeProfile x) univ c) : ∃ (i : Fin n) (left : Bool), (if left then ∀ j, x j ≤ x i else ∀ j, x i ≤ x j) ∧ IsLUB (allFreeValues x) (halfLogLik x (x i) (sqrt (endpointSquares x (x i) / n)))

statement: The exact symmetric sample has two distinct finite all-free maximizers at reflected modes. The maximizing side scales are supplied by `allFree_graph`.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: : ∃ c : ℝ, c ≠ 0 ∧ modeFraction reflectedSample c ∈ Ioo 0 1 ∧ modeFraction reflectedSample (-c) = 1 - modeFraction reflectedSample c ∧ IsMinOn (modeProfile reflectedSample) univ c ∧ IsMinOn (modeProfile reflectedSample) univ (-c)
dossier_scope_note: The rational mode 1/2 beats the center and both ends. The exact sample is the one in the written proof.

statement: With sd held, constant data give two equal half-normal traces and every finite fit has strictly lower likelihood.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {c σ : ℝ} (hσ : 0 < σ) (hx : ∀ i, x i = c) : let L := (n : ℝ) * log (halfMean * sqrt (1 - halfMean^2) / σ) (∀ d w : ℝ, w ∈ Ioo 0 1 → heldSkew x w (d, σ / sqrt (varianceFraction w)) < L) ∧ ∀ left : Bool, Tendsto (fun w ↦ heldSkew x w (c, σ / sqrt (varianceFraction w))) (𝓝[Ioo 0 1] (if left then 1 else 0)) (𝓝 L)
dossier_scope_note: Constant-data branch with sd held.

statement: With both moments held, a datum at the limiting right-half endpoint retains the exact Gaussian contact penalty as its standardized residual approaches the endpoint from the narrow side.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (μ : ℝ) {σ : ℝ} (hσ : 0 < σ) : let H := 1 - halfMean^2 let z := μ - halfMean * (σ / sqrt H) Tendsto (fun w ↦ let R := residual μ w (sqrt (varianceFraction w) / σ) z R^2 / (2 * (if R < 0 then w else 1 - w)^2)) (𝓝[Ioo 0 1] 0) (𝓝 (halfMean^2 / (8 * H^2)))
dossier_scope_note: One right contact at both fixed moments. Remaining face branches require further results.

statement: At a positive shape below one, the location minimizers are exactly the knots whose loss is smallest among the knots.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {ν : ℝ} (hν : 0 < ν) (hν' : ν < 1) (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (m : ℝ) : IsMinOn (Ged.residualSum ν x) univ m ↔ ∃ i, m = x i ∧ ∀ j, Ged.residualSum ν x (x i) ≤ Ged.residualSum ν x (x j)

statement: At positive fixed sd and shape below one, the knots of least power loss are precisely all the location maximizers.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {ν σ : ℝ} (hν : 0 < ν) (hν' : ν < 1) (hσ : 0 < σ) (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (m : ℝ) : IsMaxOn (fun t ↦ Ged.logLik ν x (t, σ)) univ m ↔ ∃ i, m = x i ∧ ∀ j, Ged.residualSum ν x (x i) ≤ Ged.residualSum ν x (x j)
dossier_scope_note: Subunit branch. The previously checked GED module handles shape one and superunit shape.

statement: With shape below one and free scale, every maximizing knot shares the same profiled scale. The sample is nonconstant so that scale is positive.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {ν : ℝ} (hν : 0 < ν) (hν' : ν < 1) (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) : Ged.jointMaximizers ν x = {p | (∃ i, p.1 = x i ∧ ∀ j, Ged.residualSum ν x (x i) ≤ Ged.residualSum ν x (x j)) ∧ p.2 = Ged.bestScale ν x p.1}
dossier_scope_note: Subunit branch. The previously checked GED module handles shape one and superunit shape.

statement: With positive sd and shape held, a maximizing location exists for every finite nonempty sample. This includes constant data and all subunit shapes.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {ν σ : ℝ} (hν : 0 < ν) (hσ : 0 < σ) (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : ∃ m, IsMaxOn (fun t ↦ Ged.logLik ν x (t, σ)) univ m

statement: At positive fixed sd and shape the log likelihood vanishes to minus infinity at either location end.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {ν σ : ℝ} (hν : 0 < ν) (hσ : 0 < σ) (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : Tendsto (fun μ ↦ Ged.logLik ν x (μ, σ)) (cocompact ℝ) atBot

statement: A rational radius and a positive rational sd cannot meet the exact real uniform contact condition. Binary64 inputs are a special case.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (r σ : ℚ) (hσ : σ ≠ 0) : (r : ℝ) ≠ sqrt 3 * (σ : ℝ)
dossier_scope_note: Arithmetic branch of the held-sd failure claim. Any finite binary64 radius or sd is rational in exact arithmetic.

statement: The positive kernel-scale parametrization is exactly the GED model.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {ν b : ℝ} (hν : 0 < ν) (hb : 0 < b) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (m : ℝ) : kernelLogLik ν x m b = Ged.logLik ν x (m, b * Ged.sdFactor ν)

statement: A vanishing relative widening approaches the unpenalized uniform value, even with observations exactly at either endpoint of the limiting interval. The fitted sd tends to the sd of that interval.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {x : Fin n → ℝ} {μ ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (h : ∀ i, |x i-μ| ≤ ρ) : let scale := fun p : ℝ ↦ (ρ * p^(1/p)) * Ged.sdFactor p Tendsto scale atTop (𝓝 (ρ / sqrt 3)) ∧ Tendsto (fun p ↦ Ged.logLik p x (μ, scale p)) atTop (𝓝 (-(n : ℝ) * log (2*ρ)))
dossier_scope_note: The sample likelihood path widens the kernel range by a vanishing amount. The argument uses free sd.

statement: If shape and both location and sd are free, allowing positive shapes below one makes the log likelihood unbounded on every nonempty sample. The construction uses reciprocal integer shapes at a sample atom.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : ¬ BddAbove {L : ℝ | ∃ ν μ σ : ℝ, 0 < ν ∧ 0 < σ ∧ L = Ged.logLik ν x (μ, σ)}

statement: Beyond the compact cutoff, a positive unavoidable radius forces every finite likelihood below the unpenalized uniform. This bound is uniform over the positive kernel scale and the location.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {μ ρ p b : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hb : 0 < b) (hp : uniformCutoff n < p) (hx : ∃ i, ρ ≤ |x i-μ|) : kernelLogLik p x μ b < -(n : ℝ) * log (2*ρ)

statement: The compact finite-shape profile decides attainment by comparison with the range uniform. The hypotheses express that the positive radius is unavoidable for the location set and encloses the data at some location.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {S : Set ℝ} (hS : IsCompact S) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hlower : ∀ μ ∈ S, ∃ i, ρ ≤ |x i-μ|) (hupper : ∃ μ ∈ S, ∀ i, |x i-μ| ≤ ρ) : let K := Icc 1 (uniformCutoff n) ×ˢ S let F := -(n : ℝ)*log (2*ρ) ∃ y ∈ K, IsMaxOn (freeSdProfile x) K y ∧ ((∃ L, IsGreatest (freeSdValues x S) L) ↔ F ≤ freeSdProfile x y) ∧ (freeSdProfile x y < F → IsLUB (freeSdValues x S) F)

statement: When the held location has a nonzero residual, the compact shape profile decides the comparison against the centered uniform.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {μ : ℝ} (hx : ∃ i, x i ≠ μ) : ∃ i : Fin n, ∀ (ρ : ℝ), ρ = |x i-μ| → 0 < ρ ∧ (∀ j, |x j-μ| ≤ ρ) ∧ ∃ y ∈ Icc 1 (uniformCutoff n) ×ˢ ({μ} : Set ℝ), IsMaxOn (freeSdProfile x) (Icc 1 (uniformCutoff n) ×ˢ {μ}) y ∧ ((∃ L, IsGreatest (freeSdValues x {μ}) L) ↔ -(n : ℝ)*log (2*ρ) ≤ freeSdProfile x y) ∧ (freeSdProfile x y < -(n : ℝ)*log (2*ρ) → IsLUB (freeSdValues x {μ}) (-(n : ℝ)*log (2*ρ)))
dossier_scope_note: Signs and attainment are decided by the compact profile. Constant data at the held mean use fitted_constant_collapse.

statement: Nonconstant data with all coefficients free are decided by the profile on the sample range and the stated compact shape interval.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) : ∃ l r : Fin n, (∀ i, x l ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ x r) ∧ let ρ := (x r-x l)/2 let K := Icc 1 (uniformCutoff n) ×ˢ Icc (x l) (x r) let F := -(n : ℝ)*log (2*ρ) ∃ y ∈ K, IsMaxOn (freeSdProfile x) K y ∧ ((∃ L, IsGreatest (freeSdValues x univ) L) ↔ F ≤ freeSdProfile x y) ∧ (freeSdProfile x y < F → IsLUB (freeSdValues x univ) F)

statement: Constant data at an admissible location have unbounded fitted-domain likelihood even if the shape restriction includes only shapes at least one.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {S : Set ℝ} {μ : ℝ} (hμ : μ ∈ S) (hx : ∀ i, x i = μ) : ¬ BddAbove (freeSdValues x S)
dossier_scope_note: Applies with free mean or with mean held at the common observation.

statement: At shape one half and held mean zero there is a valid held skew for which the sample at minus one has distinct global scale maximizers.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: : ∃ w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, ∃ u₁ u₂ : ℝ, 0 < u₁ ∧ u₁ < u₂ ∧ IsMaxOn (heldMeanSkew (fun _ : Fin 1 ↦ -1) 0 (1/2) w) (Ioi 0) u₁ ∧ IsMaxOn (heldMeanSkew (fun _ : Fin 1 ↦ -1) 0 (1/2) w) (Ioi 0) u₂
dossier_scope_note: Counterexample to the atlas uniqueness statement at all positive held shapes.

statement: With all observations at the held mean the held-shape, held-skew likelihood diverges as width vanishes.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {μ p w : ℝ} (hx : ∀ i, x i = μ) : Tendsto (heldMeanSkew x μ p w) atTop atTop

statement: A nonzero residual excludes both width ends under held mean, shape and skew, at every positive held shape.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {μ p w : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (hx : ∃ i, x i ≠ μ) : Tendsto (heldMeanSkew x μ p w) (𝓝[>] 0) atBot ∧ Tendsto (heldMeanSkew x μ p w) atTop atBot

statement: At every fixed positive shape and positive finite skew, the held-mean fit attains exactly when some residual from the held mean is nonzero.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {μ p w : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) : (∃ u ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ), IsMaxOn (heldMeanSkew x μ p w) (Ioi 0) u) ↔ ∃ i, x i ≠ μ

statement: At shapes at least one the held-mean and held-skew maximum, when it exists, is unique.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hn : 0 < n) {μ p w : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (hx : ∃ i, x i ≠ μ) : ∃! u, u ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ) ∧ IsMaxOn (heldMeanSkew x μ p w) (Ioi 0) u
dossier_scope_note: Shapes at least one. Subunit asymmetric holds can give ties.

statement: At fixed positive shape, skew and sd, likelihood tends to zero at both location ends, a maximizer always exists, and above shape one it is unique. Fixing sd fixes total width in these coordinates.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {p w s : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (hs : 0 < s) : Tendsto (fun c ↦ fixedSkewLogLik x p w (c,s)) (cocompact ℝ) atBot ∧ (∃ c, IsMaxOn (fun d ↦ fixedSkewLogLik x p w (d,s)) univ c) ∧ (1 < p → ∃! c, IsMaxOn (fun d ↦ fixedSkewLogLik x p w (d,s)) univ c)
dossier_scope_note: Fixed positive skew and shape. Holding sd fixes total kernel width and the mode is a translate of mean.

statement: Constant samples collapse at the fixed skew, with the mode set at the common observation and total kernel width tending to zero.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {p w c : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hx : ∀ i, x i = c) : Tendsto (fun u ↦ fixedSkewLogLik x p w (c,1/u)) atTop atTop

statement: Fixed positive shape and skew leave a finite joint mode and scale fit exactly on nonconstant samples. At shapes above one it is unique.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {p w : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) : ((∃ cs ∈ LocationScale.domain, IsMaxOn (fixedSkewLogLik x p w) LocationScale.domain cs) ↔ LocationScale.Nonconstant x) ∧ (LocationScale.Nonconstant x → 1 < p → ∃! cs, cs ∈ LocationScale.domain ∧ IsMaxOn (fixedSkewLogLik x p w) LocationScale.domain cs)

statement: At every shape between zero and one inclusive, this sample with unit skew gives two maximizing locations at a common positive width.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hp' : p ≤ 1) : ∃ s > 0, IsMaxOn (fixedSkewLogLik symmetricPair p (1/2)) LocationScale.domain (-1,s) ∧ IsMaxOn (fixedSkewLogLik symmetricPair p (1/2)) LocationScale.domain (1,s)

statement: The log likelihood after removal of the width exponent tends to the sharp constant along the specified fixed-shape, fixed-skew path. This includes no observations at the atom, any side count zero, and all ties.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (x : Fin n → ℝ) (y ν w e : ℝ) (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) : Tendsto (fun u ↦ logAlongAtom x y ν w e u + TDist.exponent x y ν * log u) atTop (𝓝 (collapseLogHeight x y ν w e))
dossier_scope_note: Take e=halfMoment ν*(1-2*w) for held mean or e=0 for an exact join.

statement: The sign of the collapse exponent classifies the fixed-width-fraction path at either specified offset. At equality the product likelihood has the stated strictly positive limit.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (x : Fin n → ℝ) (y ν w e : ℝ) (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) : let E := TDist.exponent x y ν let f := logAlongAtom x y ν w e (E < 0 → Tendsto f atTop atTop) ∧ (0 < E → Tendsto f atTop atBot) ∧ (E = 0 → Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 (collapseLogHeight x y ν w e)) ∧ Tendsto (fun u ↦ exp (f u)) atTop (𝓝 (exp (collapseLogHeight x y ν w e))))
dossier_scope_note: Sharp fixed-offset path values. Other moving paths require separate bounds.

statement: Infinite total width sends the log likelihood to minus infinity for every nonempty sample under fixed shape and skew.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (y ν w e : ℝ) (hν : 2 < ν) : Tendsto (logAlongAtom x y ν w e) (𝓝[>] 0) atBot

statement: The score remains valid at observations crossing the moving mode.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (x : Fin n → ℝ) (y ν w e : ℝ) (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) {u : ℝ} (hu : 0 < u) : HasDerivAt (logAlongAtom x y ν w e) (scaleScore x y ν w e u) u

statement: The held-mean, held-shape, held-skew fit exists exactly when a finite score zero reaches the collapse envelope. For a general fixed offset this is the same criterion on the resulting inverse-width ray.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (y ν w e : ℝ) (hν : 2 < ν) (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) : (∃ u ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ), IsMaxOn (logAlongAtom x y ν w e) (Ioi 0) u) ↔ ∃ u > 0, scaleScore x y ν w e u = 0 ∧ meetsCollapse x y ν w e u
dossier_scope_note: The held-mean result specializes the offset to halfMoment ν*(1-2*w).

statement: All maximizing scales are the stationary points that meet the collapse envelope and tie for the greatest stationary value.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (y ν w e : ℝ) (hν : 2 < ν) (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) {u : ℝ} (hu : 0 < u) : IsMaxOn (logAlongAtom x y ν w e) (Ioi 0) u ↔ scaleScore x y ν w e u = 0 ∧ meetsCollapse x y ν w e u ∧ ∀ v > 0, scaleScore x y ν w e v = 0 → logAlongAtom x y ν w e v ≤ logAlongAtom x y ν w e u
dossier_scope_note: Use with scaleScore_roots_finite for the finite candidate set.

statement: The inverse-width score has only finitely many positive roots. Clearing denominators on every sign assignment gives a polynomial with nonzero constant term, including assignments with zero side counts.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (y ν w e : ℝ) (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) : {u : ℝ | 0 < u ∧ scaleScore x y ν w e u = 0}.Finite

statement: At critical multiplicity on the exact-join path, the likelihood strictly increases as width shrinks and its finite supremum is unattained. Unit skew makes this the held-mean path as well.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (y ν w : ℝ) (hν : 2 < ν) (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (hE : TDist.exponent x y ν = 0) : let f := logAlongAtom x y ν w 0 let C := collapseLogHeight x y ν w 0 StrictMonoOn f (Ioi 0) ∧ IsLUB (f '' Ioi 0) C ∧ ∀ u > 0, f u < C
dossier_scope_note: At unit skew and fixed mean the offset is zero. At arbitrary skew this theorem uses an exact join.

statement: A moving join and even a vanishing side cannot increase the power of fixed-shape collapse. The width fractions may vary arbitrarily while positive, and the concentration point may be any finite real number.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} (x : Fin n → ℝ) (y ν : ℝ) (hν : 2 < ν) {u w e : ι → ℝ} (hu : Tendsto u l atTop) (hw : ∀ᶠ t in l, w t ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (he : Tendsto (fun t ↦ e t/u t) l (𝓝 (0 : ℝ))) : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ t in l, logAlongAtom x y ν (w t) (e t) (u t) ≤ -TDist.exponent x y ν * log (u t) + C
dossier_scope_note: Upper bound for fixed shape, allowing moving join and simultaneous skew degeneration. Uses fixed-shape, fixed-skew paths for sharp strict divergence.

statement: The held-mean, held-shape, held-skew likelihood is unbounded precisely at strict collapse multiplicity. The conclusion also holds on the more general fixed-offset ray.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (y ν w e : ℝ) (hν : 2 < ν) (hw : w ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) : ¬ BddAbove (logAlongAtom x y ν w e '' Ioi 0) ↔ TDist.exponent x y ν < 0
dossier_scope_note: Specialize to the held-mean offset for the strict collapse detector.
